newsitem.title: MEXICO: Fugitive Mexico drug lord said to live near capital.
newsitem.headline: Fugitive Mexico drug lord said to live near capital.

text.p: Mexico's most-wanted drug lord is not in a remote mountain or village hiding place but enjoying a luxury lifestyle at swanky homes only an hour's drive from Mexico City, Reforma newspaper said on Thursday.

Amado Carrillo Fuentes, nicknamed "Lord of the Skies" for his ability to fly jet-loads of cocaine to Mexico to smuggle into the United States, has been a fugitive for years. But Reforma said he was regularly using a mansion in the resort of Cuernavaca, 60 miles (100 km) south of Mexico City, and a ranch in the nearby village of Tetecala.

"According to residents, during at least the last five years Carrillo has been using his properties in Cuernavaca and Tetecala, in the west of the state which is governed by Jorge Carrillo Olea, the former coordinator of the fight against drug trafficking during the government of (former President) Carlos Salinas," Reforma said.

Asked about the report, a spokeswoman at Mexico's National Institute for the Combat of Drugs (INCD) said: "This is part of an investigation which the authorities are carrying out to see whether there are illicit properties of this drug trafficker. The investigation is under way and we cannot accept or deny the report."

Reforma said the drug lord's mansion in Cuernavaca was just two blocks from the offices of state Gov. Carrillo Olea. The two are not related and the newspaper did not suggest that the governor was involved with Carrillo Fuentes. No one was available at the state government's press office to comment.

"Luxury cars often drive out with darkened, bullet-proofed windows," the newspaper quoted a neighbour of the drug lord's Cuernavaca mansion as saying. "The people who open the door are strange types. They wear cowboy boots, use dark glasses and have ostentatious jewelry on their arms and neck."

Former Mexican justice officials have said Cuernavaca, a warm and sunny town where many wealthy Mexicans have weekend homes, was a haven for drugs traffickers. Attention focused on the city this month when the attorney general's office raided what it said was a wedding party for Carrillo Fuentes's sister Aurora on a ranch in the northwestern state of Sinaloa.
Agents were alerted to the "narco-wedding" when three private planes took off from Cuernavaca airport for Sinaloa without filing flight plans, the PGR said.

Reforma said Cuernavaca airport is used only by one little-known airline, which flies daily flights to Tijuana, a city on the U.S. border that is a key drug-smuggling centre. The flights stop on the way in Culiacan and Hermosillo, "cities identified with drug trafficking," the paper said.
